corrections.text: The article cites TechCrunch's September 1 report for the Fable retention case without saying that the report largely restates Anthropic's own announcement (it quotes the announcement's line that Anthropic has never trained on enterprise data without permission). It is the only outlet independent of GitHub and Anthropic cited for that case; the Grok Build, ZCode and Copilot training cases each rest on separate news outlets.

What the article says cereblab and ferstar found is taken from press reports (The Next Web, The Verge, SDxCentral, InfoWorld); the Herald did not read the researchers' own posts, and the phrase 'the researchers' accounts' in the Implications section refers to those reports. The ZCode snapshot of 42,411 files that The Next Web describes, with 564 failed upload attempts, never left ferstar's machine; The Next Web says a smaller snapshot of 538 files did reach the server.

The article says Anthropic's post 'describes a replacement, Enterprise Frontier Safeguards'. The post does not use that word: it presents EFS as a solution combining zero data retention with misuse detection, with customer-owned storage, customer-managed keys and automated review each opt-in, and says eligible customers receive zero data retention on Fable 5 and 5.1 'until EFS is ready'. That EFS is required once the zero-retention exemption ends comes from GitHub's changelog, not from Anthropic's post.
